t:
(a) Modifications to Strategic Policy.—Section 2229(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:
“(a) Policy Required.—“(1) In general.—The Secretary of Defense shall maintain a strategic policy on the programs of the Department of Defense for prepositioned materiel and equipment. Such policy shall take into account national security threats, strategic mobility, service requirements, and the requirements of the combatant commands, and shall address how the Department’s prepositioning programs, both ground and afloat, align with national defense strategies and departmental priorities.“(2) Elements.—The strategic policy required under paragraph (1) shall include the following elements:“(A) Overarching strategic guidance concerning planning and resource priorities that link the Department of Defense’s current and future needs for prepositioned stocks, such as desired responsiveness, to evolving national defense objectives.“(B) A description of the Department’s vision for prepositioning programs and the desired end state.“(C) Specific interim goals demonstrating how the vision and end state will be achieved.“(D) A description of the strategic environment, requirements for, and challenges associated with, prepositioning.“(E) Metrics for how the Department will evaluate the extent to which prepositioned assets are achieving defense objectives.“(F) A framework for joint departmental oversight that reviews and synchronizes the military services’ prepositioning strategies to minimize potentially duplicative efforts and maximize efficiencies in prepositioned materiel and equipment across the Department of Defense.“(3) Joint oversight.—The Secretary of Defense shall establish joint oversight of the military services’ prepositioning efforts to maximize efficiencies across the Department of Defense.”. 
    (b) Implementation Plan.—
        (1) In general.—Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a plan for implementation of the prepositioning strategic policy required under section 2229(a) of title 10, United States Code, as amended by subsection (a). 
        (2) Elements.—The implementation plan required under paragraph (1) shall include the following elements:
            (A) Detailed guidance for how the Department of Defense will achieve the vision, end state, and goals outlined in the strategic policy. 
            (B) A comprehensive list of the Department’s prepositioned materiel and equipment programs. 
            (C) A detailed description of how the plan will be implemented. 
            (D) A schedule with milestones for the implementation of the plan. 
            (E) An assignment of roles and responsibilities for the implementation of the plan. 
            (F) A description of the resources required to implement the plan. 
            (G) A description of how the plan will be reviewed and assessed to monitor progress.   
    (c) Comptroller General Report.—Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter, the Comptroller General of the United States shall review the implementation plan submitted under subsection (b) and the prepositioning strategic policy required under section 2229(a) of title 10, United States Code, as amended by subsection (a), and submit to the congressional defense committees a report describing the findings of such review and including any additional information relating to the propositioning strategic policy and plan that the Comptroller General determines appropriate.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the implementation plan, joint oversight, and Comptroller General review are procedural consultation steps. But every actor involved (the Secretary of Defense, the military services, the combatant commands, the Comptroller General, and the congressional defense committees) is inside the federal government. There is no public comment, rulemaking, advisory body with outside members, consultation with states or other outside entities, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a plan for implementation of the prepositioning strategic policy

opus.w: Every actor in this section is inside the federal government: the Secretary of Defense, the military services, the combatant commands, the congressional defense committees and the Comptroller General. Reports to Congress and GAO reviews are intra-government oversight, and 'joint oversight' coordinates only DoD components. No outside party is consulted, and there is no public comment, hearing, rulemaking or right to sue.
opus.s: the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a plan for implementation of the prepositioning strategic policy
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section uses process words like "joint oversight," "submit to the congressional defense committees" and a Comptroller General "review." These can look like participation. But every actor named is inside the federal government: the Secretary of Defense, the military services, the combatant commands, the congressional defense committees and the Comptroller General (who heads GAO, a legislative-branch agency). No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing, rulemaking or right to sue. So the answer is "No."

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary of Defense to maintain a strategic policy and submit reports to congressional committees. All actors involved (Secretary of Defense, military services, Comptroller General, Congress) are inside the federal government. There is no requirement to consult or coordinate with any outside parties such as states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of Defense shall establish joint oversight of the military services’ prepositioning efforts to maximize efficiencies across the Department of Defense.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "joint oversight" or "implementation plan" involves coordination with outside entities, but the text specifies "joint departmental oversight" and "military services' prepositioning strategies," which are all internal to the Department of Defense (federal government). The reports are submitted to Congress, which is also inside the federal government. There is no mention of consulting with states, tribes, the public, or private entities.
